classes.name: sandstone with shale and coal bands

stages.name: Fetch
stages.what: Pull from source archives — NASA, Copernicus, ESA, GSI, HydroSHEDS, OpenStreetMap, the state portals, and the river gauges of CWC and NWDP.
stages.note: Raw files are never edited in place, and every fetch writes its source, licence and checksum alongside.

stages.name: Align
stages.what: Reproject and resample everything onto one 100 m grid over Arunachal.
stages.note: One lattice, EPSG:32646. Every layer lines up cell for cell, which is what lets two hazards share a map.

stages.name: Feature
stages.what: Derive what the models actually read — slope, curvature, wetness, distances, rainfall percentiles.
stages.note: Terrain and soil are static and computed once; rainfall is rebuilt every day.

stages.name: Model
stages.what: Fit where-it-fails and where-it-floods on verified evidence; score today's weather and river readings against each place's own history.
stages.note: Validated by hiding whole regions during training, so scores come from ground the model has never seen.

stages.name: Export
stages.what: Cut the small web bundles the app actually reads.
stages.note: Small enough for a free host — which is why the live app carries no model files and no geospatial stack.

datasets.name: Live-rain history (Open-Meteo)
datasets.note: The same source the live forecast reads each morning, so a day's rain is scored against its own history.

datasets.name: Soil wetness (ERA5-Land)
datasets.note: Read by the flood forecast on flat ground.

datasets.name: River levels (CWC)
datasets.note: The history the river models learned from. New readings are read live at every forecast run.

datasets.name: River flows (NWDP)
datasets.note: The history the river models learned from. New readings are read live at every forecast run; this network publishes about 2 days late. 4 readings carry a much earlier date in the source and are left out of the span.

datasets.name: Radar scenes (Sentinel-1)
datasets.note: Scenes on and around flood dates.

datasets.name: Flood reports to check
datasets.note: Candidates only: a report counts once radar, a satellite flood map or a gauge confirms it.

datasets.name: Verified flood record
datasets.note: Confirmed by: radar 1,153, gfd 1,016, gauge 71, gauge-xc 59. Rebuilt by hand; what the daily run finds (a gauge crossing its line, a confirmed report) is logged beside it and joins at the next rebuild.

datasets.name: River readings logged live
datasets.note: What the gauges read on each forecast day — the readings forecasts are graded against.

datasets.name: Flood forecast log
datasets.note: 1,564 graded against the gauges so far.

models.name: Landslide — where
models.what: Where slopes fail, from mapped landslides.

models.name: Landslide — when
models.what: How unusual today's rain is for each place.

models.name: Flood — when
models.what: The chance of a flood near a place on a day.

models.name: Flood — where
models.what: Where water goes if a flood comes.

models.name: River — chance of reaching its line
models.what: One model per day ahead, 9 days, 32 gauges.

models.name: River — level
models.what: The river's daily high; drawn 2 days ahead.

privacy.rule: No source dataset can be reconstructed from this bundle.
privacy.histograms: 28 bins per layer — shape only, no cell values
privacy.thumbnails: ~98 px wide, about 6 km per pixel, 8-bit
privacy.demo_rows: Synthetic. Each column drawn independently from its own marginal, so no row is a real location.
